headline_marked: [[MaxFi's zero-swap]] rebalancing risks major losses in one-way markets
headline: MaxFi's zero-swap rebalancing risks major losses in one-way markets
summary: While MaxFi's zero-swap rebalancing offers advantages, it can lead to significant losses if prices trend downwards without a bounce-back.
details: Active liquidity management in DeFi has three main tools: VFat, Krystal, and the newer MaxFi. While VFat and Krystal use traditional swap-based rebalancing, MaxFi employs a zero-swap rebalancing logic that repositions ranges without trading assets.

VFat and Krystal's swap-based approach involves selling one token to buy another when a position goes out of range. This occurs at price extremes, incurring costs and crystallizing impermanent loss, which is permanently locked in.

MaxFi's zero-swap rebalancing defers impermanent loss by re-anchoring the range using existing tokens. This method excels in mean-reverting markets where prices quickly bounce back, allowing users to collect fees throughout.

However, MaxFi's zero-swap mechanic poses a significant risk in one-way down markets. Unlike swap-based tools that partially protect capital by converting to stablecoins, zero-swap tools leave users fully exposed to the depreciating asset.

Historically, major cryptocurrencies like ETH have experienced drops of 50% or more. In such scenarios, a zero-swap tool would have kept users entirely in the falling asset, with no hedge and no improvement in average entry price.

Furthermore, in a one-way down market, zero-swap tools result in 'dead time' where positions earn no LP fees as they sit below the active range. Fees are only collected again once the price reverses and re-enters the range.
